title: Redo role-prompt goal-preservation change; fix every stale 1,800 mention
summary: Redo the rejected job from the base: edit the reader, producer and verifier prompts so the request's real goal survives to the verdict, make a non-empty request_reading_mismatch a Major finding in judge(), raise the reader budget minimally. This time grep every 1,800 mention, including socratic-review.md:176, and rewrap edited lines to file width.

defaults_applied.how: Grep every statement of the 1,800 budget across docs and code, then re-run the grep to show no stale present-tense hits remain.
Add unit tests in verify.rs for mismatch present and absent or blank; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
decisions.md records the measured reader count and why removals cannot pay for the new rules.
One change, limited to the three prompts, judge(), the budget and its documents.
The mismatch-as-Major rule is enforced in judge() code, not only in prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience for this change is the maintainers and the Athena roles that read these prompts and docs; the earlier reading's criteria stand.

The prior rejections' findings are the checked list: socratic-review.md:176 (and :219, :198 if present tense), decision-sets.md:111 and defaults-loop.md:227 over-wide lines, and the decision-sets.md:111 nit mixing current numbers into a dated review-1 measurement.
Past-tense review and history records (docs/design/reviews/*, decisions.md:1971, defaults-loop.md:227's review-1 measurement) may keep 1,800 as dated facts; timeout_s 1800 is unrelated.
The new budget is the measured count of the new reader set plus minimal headroom, as in the earlier attempt (about 1,910).

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md tells the reader to name the request's audience (who will use or judge the result) in the summary or assumptions.
reader.md requires at least one acceptance criterion written as an outcome the named audience can check; presence checks alone do not satisfy it.
reader.md forbids putting the request's own stated goal in out_of_scope, and tells the reader to read the current output the request is about before planning a change to it.
producer.md treats the acceptance criteria as a floor and tells the producer to serve the request's goal, while keeping the small-change and follow-conventions instructions.
verifier.md tells the verifier to judge user-facing output as its intended audience would, and to rate a request-reading mismatch at least major, never minor because the criteria passed.

In judge() in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, a non-empty request_reading_mismatch adds a Major finding and a reason, so the verdict is not pass. Unit tests cover mismatch present and absent or blank. Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify
The BudgetSet::Reader budget is raised only as far as the new reader text needs. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
docs/decisions.md records the new reader budget, the measured count and why removals cannot pay for the new rules; CHANGELOG.md notes the change.

A repo-wide Grep for 1,800 and 1800 finds no present-tense statement of the old reader budget: defaults-loop.md:47, :227, :413; decision-sets.md:107, :111; decisions.md:612; athena-v0.md:1507, :1868; socratic-review.md:176, :198 if present tense, :219 are updated. Past-tense review and history records may keep it.

No rewritten doc line is much wider than its file's wrapping (Grep for lines of 125 or more characters on the edited lines finds none newly added), and dated review-1 measurements stay purely past figures rather than mixing in the new budget.
The workspace stays clean and tested. Run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test

out_of_scope: Changing past-tense review and history records that cite 1,800 as a dated measurement
Changing the job loop, a repair loop, or rejection events (a separate design change)
Edits to records/ or the owner's files
departures: Cost and time are above the reference: the change touches about a dozen files, including prompts, a budget and a doc-wide sweep, and the same job was rejected twice before.
